subject: NCCL/RCCL channel-and-buffer registration as a one-time modeled time cost gating first use, under the interim constant-completion contract

fatal_guards.claim: the default-constructed arm and the explicitly disabled arm agree field by field
every GOAL artifact SHA-256 is identical between the off and on arms
the off arm reproduces the accepted baseline timings exactly
every step and every request partition conserves its span exactly
a calibrated request against a declared cost fails closed
no collective is charged registration on more than one artifact
the mirrored nccl_stack event stream is unchanged when no registration is requested
the results identity block equals this freeze
ledger construction facts: first charge pays, second charges zero, new buffer, new peer and bumped generation each re-pay, disabled charges zero

rows.claim: decode-step makespans are unchanged between on and off
a rebuild re-pays exactly once on step 2 and leaves TTFT at the plain on-arm value
TTFT_on - TTFT_off == 80000000 across a phase-split collective with a real backend
the published registration component equals the ledger charge per step

families.claim: charged registration is exactly identities x 20000000 ps
the charge is additive on top of the composed service, never absorbed by the max term
steps after the registering step are untouched

not_established: no calibration of the registration cost
no deregistration, cache eviction or size dependence
no evidence about whether the no-tail constant completion is the right collective model
